titles: Why Your Spouse Got the Bigger Refund: Tuition Transfer ($725) | Canada Tax
Transfer Tuition to Your Spouse: Up to $5,000 (Canada 2025)
Student Spouse Owes $0 Tax? Move the Tuition Credit (Line 32600)
yt.description:
Sam paid the tuition. Alex got the bigger refund: $725 bigger. And that's the plan.

The example (federal, 2025): Sam went back to school with $8,000 of tuition and $12,000 of income, under the basic personal amount ($16,129), so Sam owes $0 federal tax and the tuition credit has nothing to cut.

The rule (line 32600, Schedule 2): a spouse or common-law partner can claim up to $5,000 of the student's current-year tuition, minus what the student needs to bring their own tax to zero.
• Sam needs $0 → Alex claims $5,000 × 14.5% = $725 off federal tax

The twist: the other $3,000 stays with Sam as a carry-forward and can never be transferred later. Unused age, pension and disability amounts can move to a spouse the same way.

Do the lower-income return first, and see what's left to transfer.

Next: why the Canada Child Benefit goes to one parent.

Sources: canada.ca (CRA) line 32600; tuition transfer rules (line 32400 page); What's new for 2025. Federal only; provincial amounts differ. Example. General information, not advice.
